domain_setting: Everyday connections across a welcoming home, neighborhood, workplace, and public places. Family members, friends, neighbors, coworkers, and partners show relationships through supportive shared moments and clear emotional distance.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use varied people and ages in natural everyday places, with relationships clear through shared attention, resemblance, support, or separation.
Use home, neighborhood walks, workplaces, parks, cafes, and quiet public places as a coherent modern community setting.
Give each friendship and relationship verb a distinct physical action or interaction rather than repeating generic smiling pairs.
Keep dating, family, friendship, coworker, and neighbor relationships distinct; avoid stereotypes and avoid written labels, speech bubbles, or readable screens.

polysemy_resolution_table.families: People related across generations in a warm shared moment, not a business or animal classification.
polysemy_resolution_table.bring someone up / bring up someone: Care for and raise a child over time, not lifting a person physically or bringing up a topic.
polysemy_resolution_table.give birth: A parent resting safely with a newborn after delivery, shown non-graphically in a hospital.
polysemy_resolution_table.grow up: The same person progressing from childhood to adulthood, not merely growing taller in one instant.
polysemy_resolution_table.run in the family: A visible feature shared across generations, not a person running.
polysemy_resolution_table.take after someone: A child visibly resembling one parent, distinct from a trait shared by a whole family line.
polysemy_resolution_table.relationship / relationships: Family ties among relatives, matching the Japanese gloss; not a romantic relationship alone.
polysemy_resolution_table.date: A calendar date, matching the Japanese gloss, not a romantic outing.

contrast_notes.run in the family / take after someone: Run in the family uses three generations sharing one feature; take after someone focuses on a single child-parent resemblance.
contrast_notes.best friend / close friend / make friend: Best friend is a trusted long-term pair, close friend is warm existing familiarity, and make friends captures a first welcoming introduction.
contrast_notes.get along / get along with someone / cli: Show, respectively, cooperative ease, a specific harmonious pair, instant rapport, and a concrete shared interest.
contrast_notes.break up / break up with someone / drift: Use a mutual parting, a clear conversation ending a couple relationship, gradual physical distance, and a disagreement between former friends.
contrast_notes.put your foot down: A person firmly sets a boundary with a grounded stance and calm raised palm, not literally stepping on an object.
